$comment: The toolchain the CI build legs and the nightly analysis jobs are pinned to, in one place. tests/toolchain/check_versions.cmake fails if .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/analysis.yml, .github/requirements/analysis.txt or the vcpkg pin drifts from this file (docs/ci.md). qt.action is the install-qt-action pin; qt.aqtsource is the aqtinstall commit it installs from git instead of PyPI, because Qt split the Windows repository per architecture from 6.11 and the last PyPI release (3.3.0) cannot read it (docs/ci.md, 'Qt on the Windows leg').

android.$comment: What the Android build installs beside Qt's Android kit. The NDK is the one the kit is built with (its qt.toolchain.cmake names r27c, which is 27.2.12479018), not the newest the runner image carries; the platform is the newest Google Play takes as a target level; the JDK is the one Gradle needs (the runner image's). .github/workflows/android-build.yml and the android job of release.yml carry the same values, and tests/platform/check_android.cmake holds them to this file.

emscripten.$comment: What the web build installs beside Qt's WebAssembly kit. The version is the one the kit asks for (its QtPublicWasmToolchainHelpers.cmake: QT_EMCC_RECOMMENDED_VERSION, 5.0.5 for Qt 6.12.0), not the newest the infra's setup-emscripten action defaults to; the commit is the emsdk repository's tag of that version (git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/emscripten-core/emsdk.git). The kit is the single-threaded one: a page can use threads only if it is served with cross-origin isolation headers, which GitHub Pages cannot send (docs/building.md, 'Web').
